Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

this update is about the power connection at the east loop campsite, mainly pitch 27 and pedestal P-14. the site was occupied by Mara Ellis and Tom Vale from friday 12 june until monday morning, and they reported that the supply had stopped twice during their stay. their first report came to the office at 8:20 on saturday. they said the socket was working when they arrived, and they had not moved the caravan after setting it up. the second interruption was reported just after 6 on sunday evening. both reports were entered against P-14, although the visitors were not sure if the two interruptions had the same cause.

on saturday, grounds assistant Leon Price went to pitch 27 after the first call. he found the caravan lead connected firmly to the lower socket and the pedestal breaker in the off position. he reset the breaker once, and the supply returned while he was there. Leon wrote that the breaker stayed on for the rest of his visit, which lasted about twelve minutes. he did not unplug the caravan lead, open the pedestal casing, or test the socket with another appliance. so the office record confirms a reset and a temporary return of power, but it does not establish why the breaker had operated.

Mara told the office that they were running the small refrigerator, two lamps and a phone charger at the time. she said they had not used the kettle or portable heater before the first interruption. On Sunday, she reported that the refrigerator had stopped again, but she did not know exactly when the power went off. Tom said the lamps were still on earlier in the evening and then went out together. They had no separate meter reading, and neither visitor could say whether the interruption lasted a few minutes or longer. The office asked them to leave the breaker alone if it tripped again and to call rather than trying repeated resets.

1. the site record shows the following for the booking:
   - pitch: 27, east loop
   - connection: pedestal P-14, lower socket
   - arrival: friday 12 june, after 3 p.m.
   - departure: monday 15 june, before 10 a.m.
   - reports received: saturday at 8:20 a.m. and sunday just after 6 p.m.

2. the record does not include a measured load for the caravan, a photograph of the socket, or a test of the visitors' lead. It also does not say whether another pitch using P-14 had a supply problem during those dates. No other report was entered for the east loop over that weekend, but that only reflects calls made to the office, not a check with every occupied pitch.

On Monday at 9:40, electrician Nisha Cole inspected P-14 while the pitch was vacant. She saw no visible scorching or cracked plastic on the pedestal exterior. She tested the socket with the site tester and recorded a normal reading at that time. She operated the pedestal breaker twice during the check; it remained on both times. Nisha did not have Mara and Tom's caravan or lead available, so she could not reproduce the reported interruption with their equipment. Her note says, “No fault found during the visit; intermittent operation cannot be ruled out.” The inspection was limited to the pedestal and its socket, and no cable was opened or replaced.

Nisha also checked the distribution board serving the east loop. The labelled circuit for P-14 was in the on position, and its indicator showed no active trip when she arrived. She did not test every outlet supplied by that circuit, or inspect the buried cable between the board and pedestal. Her visit lasted about twenty-five minutes, including the socket test and the board check. The site log has no earlier maintenance entry for P-14 this season, but older paper records are held separately and have not yet been checked for this update.

The campsite office has left P-14 available for booking because the Monday test showed power at the socket and no visible damage was noted. This is the current booking status, not a claim that the reported interruptions have been explained. Staff were asked to tell the next guests at pitch 27 to contact the office promptly if the supply stops, and not to reset the breaker more than once. The request applies to that pitch while the report is being followed up; it is not a change to the instructions for every pedestal on the site. The office has not promised a repair date or told the visitors that the issue is resolved.

The next check is conditional on getting access to the visitors' lead and, if possible, the caravan or an equivalent load. Mara said she could bring the lead to the office after work on Wednesday, but she had not confirmed a time. If it is brought in, Nisha plans to inspect it before using it in a test at P-14. If she cannot arrange the equipment, she will instead return to the pedestal during the next occupied period and ask the guests to call while the problem is happening. That would still not establish whether the caravan's own equipment was involved unless it could be checked as well.

The reception ledger also records that pitch 26 was occupied on both Saturday and Sunday, but no one staying there reported a loss of power. The ledger gives no information about what equipment was used at pitch 26, and staff did not ask those guests whether they noticed a brief interruption. A booking for pitch 27 is due to arrive on Friday, subject to the normal site opening schedule.
